selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main subject introduced at the beginning of the marked passage?
questions.answer: It introduces a reflection on how a person searching the universe can come to know his Creator.

questions.question: Why is the world compared to several different kinds of places instead of just one?
questions.answer: To show that it serves many purposes at once, such as nourishment, beauty, learning, and discipline.

questions.question: What limitation of human beings is mentioned in that verse?
questions.answer: People often do not understand how creation glorifies Allah.

questions.question: What does the image of a school suggest about the world?
questions.answer: It suggests that the world teaches those who reflect on it.

questions.question: What does the traveler see in the heavens besides beauty?
questions.answer: He sees active rule, control, movement, and service being carried out.

questions.question: What signs of wisdom are seen in the heavens?
questions.answer: The system is balanced, regular, coordinated, and free from disorder.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the orderly movement of the heavenly bodies?
questions.answer: They are compared to a disciplined army carrying out commands.

questions.question: Why mention the cleaning of the heavens?
questions.answer: To show that the cosmos is actively maintained, not merely set in motion and left alone.

questions.question: What role does the earth’s motion play in the traveler’s observation?
questions.answer: It makes the sky appear in new forms night by night and season by season.

questions.question: What false idea is challenged by the detailed order described in the heavens?
questions.answer: The idea that the universe runs aimlessly or without a governing will is challenged.

questions.question: What Qur’anic idea is placed at the start of the marked passage?
questions.answer: It states that the heavens, the earth, and everything in them glorify Allah, even if people do not fully grasp that praise.

questions.question: What basic questions does the traveler ask when he first opens his eyes to the world?
questions.answer: He asks who owns and governs this world and who brought such an ordered realm into being.

questions.question: Why do the heavens answer that search before anything else in the passage?
questions.answer: Their scale, beauty, and visibility make them the most immediate and striking sign.

questions.question: Why are the heavens described as a “page” in effect?
questions.answer: Because they can be read as a visible sign that points to divine unity.

questions.question: What invitation do the heavens seem to give the traveler?
questions.answer: They invite him to examine them so they can guide him toward the truth he is seeking.

questions.question: Why is the phrase about no supporting pillar significant?
questions.answer: It highlights the extraordinary nature of the heavens being sustained by divine power rather than visible props.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the sun and moon carry out their duties without rebellion?
questions.answer: It portrays them as obedient parts of a greater order established by their Creator.

questions.question: What effect is created by the many examples of order, movement, and control in the heavens?
questions.answer: They lead the reader to infer deliberate rule, wisdom, and purposeful governance.

questions.question: What is gained by comparing the sky to a screen with scenes appearing on it?
questions.answer: The comparison highlights ongoing variety and purposeful presentation.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is the core message of the marked passage?
questions.answer: Careful reflection on the heavens leads a sincere person to recognize the wise, powerful, and sovereign Creator.

questions.question: What title is given to this section of the work?
questions.answer: It is presented as a supreme sign explored through the observations of a questioning traveler.

questions.question: Who is the central human figure in this passage?
questions.answer: A traveler who observes the world and searches for his Maker.

questions.question: Why do the heavens have a special place at the start of the discussion?
questions.answer: They are presented as a clear and beautiful sign that points people toward Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What specific observation shows that the heavenly system is stable?
questions.answer: Huge bodies remain suspended and continue their motions without collapse or conflict.
